steps.title: Definition
steps.body: A training year (macrocycle) is divided into distinct phases, each with specific training goals. The training programme is structured so the athlete peaks (reaches their best performance) at the right time - usually for the most important competitions.

steps.title: Goal
steps.body: Build a base of fitness and develop the specific skills needed for the upcoming competitive season. The aim is to prepare the body and mind for the demands of competition.

steps.title: Goal
steps.body: Maintain the fitness built in pre-season while performing at the highest possible level in competitions. Training shifts from building fitness to maintaining it and peaking for key events.

steps.title: Tapering
steps.body: A planned reduction in training volume (by 40-60%) in the 7-14 days before a major competition. Intensity may remain high but the total training load is reduced. This allows the body to fully recover, replenish energy stores and repair any remaining muscle damage, so the athlete is at peak physical and mental condition for competition.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Know the three phases in order: pre-season → competition → post-season For each phase, state the goal, training volume, intensity and focus Tapering = reducing training before big events (important Higher-tier concept) Active recovery in post-season prevents reversibility while allowing rest Be ready to compare training programmes across phases for a specific sport Remember: pre-season builds fitness, competition season maintains it, post-season recovers
